rows.subtype: Boss expects excellence or expects nothing [Receiver]
rows.description: One intern whose manager visibly expects great work gets stretch tasks and honest feedback and rises; another treated as filler receives none of these and coasts.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A manager notices they hand the tough assignments to one person and the routine ones to another, then deliberately gives all the same challenge, feedback and patience and judges by evidence.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Parent who is sure of what the child is [Actor]
rows.description: A parent convinced their child is "the shy one" answers for them and shields them from chances; the child adopts the role, whereas expecting growth gives room to grow.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Small treat seems big or small by comparison [Actor]
rows.description: A child feels happy with a modest biscuit after getting a plain one, but tearful when a sibling gets a bigger one; the same treat feels different depending on what it is compared with.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student with a fair score feels miserable after a friend's top mark but delighted on hearing the class average was low; the reference point changed the feeling, not the marks.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Feeling plain after scrolling edited photos [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager feels unattractive after an hour of polished, filtered images, then feels normal among classmates in person; the comparison set, not the face, shifted.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Bargain looks cheap next to a costly item [Observer]
rows.description: A shopper sees a friend feel that a mid-priced shirt is cheap after looking at an expensive jacket, though it is still costly; judgments follow the last thing seen.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: An adult asks what the option is worth by itself and against their own past and needs, not just against the closest example, and avoids sizing up their life against a curated highlight reel.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Combo choice pushed by a pointless third option [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager picks the mid-size popcorn combo because a poor third option makes it look like a bargain; the choice feels smart though the decoy shaped it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult chooses the premium plan because the middle plan is barely cheaper and offers much less; the odd option made premium look like obvious value.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
